newsitem.title: GERMANY: Thyssen to make cash bid for G&L.
newsitem.headline: Thyssen to make cash bid for G&L.

text.p: German steel and engineering group Thyssen AG said on Thursday that it would make a cash bid for Giddings & Lewis, valuing the U.S. machine tool maker at $21 per share, or $700 million overall.
Thyssen said in a statement that Giddings & Lewis management would recommend to shareholders to accept the bid.

Thyssen said that the bid, to be made by its Thyssen Holding Corporation unit, would come within the next few days. Once a majority stake is acquired, Giddings & Lewis would be integrated into the core operations of Thyssen Industrie AG.

"Thyssen and G&L are convinced that joining forces would benefit both sides, because there is an excellent basis to build a technological team and significant synergy effects can be achieved," the Thyssen statement continued.

G&L has annual turnover of around $700 million, making it the biggest machine tool maker in the U.S. Around half of its sales are to the auto industry. The company has eight plants in the U.S., and one each in Canada, Germany and Britain.
G&L shares closed unchanged at $19 in New York on Wednesday.
